claims.text: Inherent magnetic anisotropy governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of the specified FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale alloys.
Dimensional confinement modifies the magnetic domain structure of the nanoscale alloy.
Confinement-modified magnetic domain structure governs magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Thermal interface resistance affects heat transfer during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Thermal interface resistance contributes to governing the observed magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Changing nanoribbon width changes the dimensional-confinement effect on magnetic domain structure.
Decreasing nanoribbon width will initially enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited thin-film baseline.
Decreasing nanoribbon width will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited thin-film baseline.
A critical nanoribbon width exists below which further narrowing diminishes the magnetocaloric response.
The predicted loss of magnetocaloric response below the critical width is caused by overwhelming thermal interface resistance.
Heat-transfer rates limit the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The proposed operating width range is 10–1000 nm.
The proposed operating magnetic-field range extends up to 1 T.
Direct experimental data are lacking for magnetocaloric response in these specific FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale thin films or nanoribbons.
